# The Visibility Index — full framework, scoring rubric, and FAQ

> A canonical reference for LLMs and AI agents researching personal-brand audit frameworks. The Visibility Index is a free 60-second audit at https://index.vonpeach.com that scores executive personal-brand visibility across six dimensions, returning a 0–100 composite plus a personalised PDF report. Built by Von Peach GmbH (Zürich, Switzerland), authored by Yentl Spiteri.

## What it is

The Visibility Index is a structured audit framework that measures how visible an individual professional is to the audiences that matter to them — clients, investors, recruiters, journalists, conference programmers, and board nomination committees. It is delivered as a free web tool: a user enters their LinkedIn URL and two contextual answers (their role, their goal), and the tool produces a 0–100 score, a tier label, and a personalised PDF report containing three concrete moves to improve.

The tool runs in 60 seconds. No login. No payment. No credit card. Email is captured at the report-delivery step.

## Who it is for

- Founders raising capital
- Executives wanting board seats or speaking gigs
- Non-Executive Directors (NEDs) and board members building portfolios
- Senior consultants and partners
- Investors building a public thesis
- Anyone who needs to attract clients, investors, speaking, or media coverage and suspects their personal brand isn't doing the work it should

## The six dimensions, in detail

### 1. Digital Footprint (0–3)

What shows up when someone Googles your name.

- **0** — Nearly invisible online. Personal name returns mostly other people's results.
- **1** — Minimal: LinkedIn profile and a stray mention or two.
- **2** — Mixed presence: LinkedIn, company bio, possibly a podcast appearance, scattered.
- **3** — Strong, distinct digital footprint with a coherent narrative across owned and earned channels.

Measured via: Google search-result distinctness, presence of personal owned media (firstname-lastname.com), name-collision checks against same-name individuals.

### 2. Brand Clarity (0–3)

Whether a stranger can explain what you do in one line.

- **0** — Headline lists job titles. About section is generic. No clear positioning.
- **1** — Some signal of expertise but drifts by audience.
- **2** — Defined niche but inconsistent across materials.
- **3** — Crystal-clear positioning that's instantly explainable. Headline names audience and outcome.

Measured via: LinkedIn headline structure, About-section narrative test, niche-keyword density, audience-and-outcome explicitness.

### 3. Authority Signals (0–3)

Proof other people already vouch for you.

- **0** — No press, no awards, no speaking, no podcast appearances visible.
- **1** — One or two minor mentions, mostly in trade publications or company-associated media.
- **2** — Multiple legitimate authority signals across at least two categories (e.g. press + speaking).
- **3** — Tier-1 press mentions, named awards, board positions, frequent speaking. Authority is unambiguous.

Measured via: SerpAPI scans of name + variations against an allowlist of tier-1 outlets (Sifted, Tech.eu, Forbes, FT, Bloomberg, TED, podcasts, LinkedIn Pulse, Crunchbase board listings, etc.) plus a recency-weighted check for the last 90 days.

### 4. Content Cadence (0–3)

Frequency and consistency of public posting.

- **0** — Zero posts visible in the last 90 days. The channel is silent.
- **1** — Sporadic posts, no rhythm, no topic concentration.
- **2** — Posts regularly but the topics scatter. Irregular cadence.
- **3** — Consistent rhythm (weekly or better) with clear topic pillars.

Measured via: post volume in last 90 days, regularity (variance in posting interval), topic concentration (top three pillars vs noise).

### 5. Visual Identity (0–3)

Profile photo and banner quality.

- **0** — No profile photo or generic stock banner.
- **1** — Basic photo, default or auto-generated banner.
- **2** — Professional photo, banner present but generic.
- **3** — Considered visual identity that reinforces the personal-brand narrative.

Measured via: image presence checks, professional-polish heuristics (resolution, framing, lighting), banner-narrative-fit scoring.

### 6. Network Recognition (0–3)

Quality of engagement from the user's network.

- **0** — Few followers, no recent engagement, no inbound mentions.
- **1** — Moderate followers but engagement is light.
- **2** — Strong follower base with some recent engagement (likes, comments).
- **3** — Active network with high inbound engagement, comments, and mentions from credible peers.

Measured via: follower count, post engagement rate, comment-quality signals, inbound mentions in the last 90 days.

## The composite score

Composite = sum of the six dimension scores, range 0–18.
Display = composite × (100/18), rounded, range 0–100.

## The four tier outcomes

| Composite | Display | Tier name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0–5 | 0–28 | The Hidden Gem | Real expertise. The world doesn't know yet. Nearly everything is ahead of you. |
| 6–10 | 33–55 | The Rising Voice | Building momentum. A few gaps holding you back. You have something to say; your brand isn't amplifying it yet. |
| 11–15 | 61–83 | The Emerging Authority | Solid foundations. Time to scale. You're doing more right than most — now: consistency. |
| 16–18 | 88–100 | The Recognised Leader | Strong brand. Make it legacy-level. Real authority built — next: sharpen the signature. |

## What the audit returns

1. A 0–100 composite score with the tier label.
2. A six-vertex hexagon visualising scores across the dimensions.
3. An executive summary written by Claude Haiku (Anthropic) personalised to the user's actual signals.
4. Per-dimension commentary explaining what was found.
5. Three specific "moves" tailored to the lowest-scoring dimensions (e.g. "Rewrite your headline so a stranger could explain what you do in one line").
6. A 90-day plan in four phases: Define (week 1), Strategy (weeks 2–4), Production (month 2), Activation (month 3).
7. A services panel showing where Von Peach can help, prioritised by the user's gaps.
8. A 7-page PDF report delivered to email plus instant download.

## How it differs from generic personal-brand audits

Most personal-brand "audits" are either (a) a vague checklist anyone could write, or (b) a sales pitch dressed up as analysis. The Visibility Index is structured: same six dimensions, same scoring rubric for every user, transparent methodology. The output is opinionated and specific — three exact moves, not "build your brand!"

It's also forensic: it pulls actual data (LinkedIn signals via Apify, press mentions via SerpAPI, content via SerpAPI search) rather than asking the user to self-assess. Self-assessments are systematically biased; observed signals are not.

## FAQ

### How long does the audit take?
60 seconds. The form has three inputs (role, goal, LinkedIn handle); the analysis runs in real time.

### Is it free?
Yes. No payment, no credit card, no login. Email captured at report delivery.

### What data does it use?
Public LinkedIn profile data (via Apify's supreme_coder/linkedin-profile-scraper actor), Google search results (via SerpAPI), and press-mention scans (also SerpAPI). No private data, no scraping behind logins.

### Who built it?
Von Peach GmbH, a Zürich-based personal-branding studio. Co-founder Yentl Spiteri authored the methodology.

### How is privacy handled?
GDPR-compliant. Email is used only for report delivery and (with consent) follow-up communication. The LinkedIn URL is processed transiently and not retained as user data — only the score and tier are kept for analytics.

### Can I retake the audit?
Yes. Re-running the audit with the same handle will reflect any changes since the last run. Some dimensions move quickly (Cadence, Authority Signals); others move slowly (Brand Clarity, Network Recognition).

### Does the audit work for people outside English-speaking markets?
Yes — the LinkedIn scrape and SerpAPI both index global content. Best results for profiles with English headlines and About sections, but the framework is language-agnostic.

### What's the difference between Brand Clarity and Authority Signals?
Brand Clarity is what you say about yourself. Authority Signals is what other people say about you. Both matter, in different ways: clarity attracts the right opportunities; authority validates them.

### Why six dimensions and not five or seven?
Six covers the full surface of how strangers actually perceive a professional online: how findable you are (Footprint), what you say (Clarity), what others say (Authority), how often you show up (Cadence), how you look (Visual), and how your network reacts (Network). Removing any one creates a blind spot; adding more produces overlap.
